correctness.rationale: For a candidate fort with side-index sets P and Q, an outside a_i has |Q|−1_{i∈Q} neighbors in the fort, with the symmetric expression for outside b_j. Every one-side triple is a fort and each of its nonempty proper subsets has an outside vertex of opposite color with exactly one neighbor. If both sides have size at most two and |P|=2, the fort condition forces P⊆Q, hence P=Q; the reverse applies if |Q|=2. If both sides have size at most one, use an unused index to find an opposite outside vertex adjacent to a singleton. The matched double-pairs are forts with no smaller fort. A missed fort prevents the first force into it, and any failed maximal forcing process leaves a missed fort. This gives exactly the three omission restrictions. Equivalently, enumerate omissions by squaring z^n+n z^(n−1)+binom(n,2) z^(n−2) and subtract the binom(n,2) aligned complements at degree 2n−4. Expansion and binom(n,2)(binom(n,2)−1)=n(n−1)(n−2)(n+1)/4 verify all coefficients and the minimum claim, including n=4.
residual_risks: Replay with python3 verify.py checks defined forts, propagation and coefficients only for n=3 through 7. The general conclusion follows from the exact neighbor-count proof.

evidence: A white set has a nonforcing blue complement exactly when it contains a fort: the process either stops with such a subset or cannot enter a missed fort. Thus the inclusion-minimal such white sets are exactly the minimal forts.
Under the prior criterion the inclusion-minimal failures are the one-side triples and the aligned pairs of indices on both sides.

value.rationale: The crown family and its minimal forts are natural, but the exact polynomial and full set criterion are already available. The remaining presentation as three minimal-fort families is a direct minimal-obstruction extraction from that criterion, not an independently useful unknown invariant under this review standard. No separable new valuable claim survives in the frozen result.
residual_risks: The direct fort proof may be useful as exposition; this is not a claim that the underlying graph invariant lacks mathematical interest.
